title: Payload size enforcement on ingestion
user_story: As an operator, I need the server to reject oversized payloads before they consume memory or disk space so that the system stays within bounded resource usage.
description: Enforce the --max-payload configuration limit on the ingestion endpoint. Use tower-http's RequestBodyLimitLayer applied to the ingestion route to reject bodies that exceed the configured max_payload size. When the limit is exceeded, return a 413 Payload Too Large with a structured JSON error including the configured limit and a suggestion to reduce payload size or adjust --max-payload. The limit must come from Config, not be hardcoded.

acceptance_criteria.when: sending a request to /h/{hook_id} with a 2000-byte body
acceptance_criteria.then: response is 413 with structured JSON error including size info and suggestion to configure --max-payload

acceptance_criteria.when: sending a request to /h/{hook_id} with a 1024-byte body
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is accepted and stored (200)

acceptance_criteria.when: sending a request to /h/{hook_id} with an empty body
acceptance_criteria.then: the request is accepted and stored (200)

acceptance_criteria.when: sending a request with a body under 1MB

acceptance_criteria.then: the response is a structured JSON error (not Axum's default plain-text 413)
tests verify rejection of oversized payloads and acceptance of payloads at and below the limit

functions.name: RequestBodyLimitLayer
functions.description: Tower layer that rejects request bodies exceeding the specified size

single_binary_checklist.notes: Payload limit prevents memory exhaustion. Rejection happens before body is fully read. Limit comes from Config.
